subject: Hosted API capacity bump & tier remap — Nimbus Commerce
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@teamnimbus.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API capacity bump & tier remap — Nimbus Commerce

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for the sync last week. Per our discussion, I put together a short proposal to map Nimbus's seasonal growth into a predictable commit and a new usage tier that reduces token unit cost once the new threshold is hit. High level:

- Monthly committed throughput: move from current 10M tokens/month to 30M tokens/month (3x).
- New soft-burst allowance: +20% monthly buffer for seasonal spikes for the first 3 months.
- Rateband remap: introduce a new mid-tier rate (Tier B) between your current Tier A and Tier C with a 12% unit-cost reduction for usage above 30M tokens.

Attached is a short worksheet with the projected month-over-month token usage (based on the June snapshot you shared), a pricing summary, and an ops checklist for provisioning. If the numbers look reasonable I can loop in Ben and Karithik to confirm discounts and finalize a PO path.

Ask: would you be able to confirm procurement readiness by next Wednesday (7/22)? Once we have verbal OK we can provision a reserved pool and do a staged rollout to avoid throttling during your peak windows.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0147
Attachment: redwood_capacity_plan_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 78KB)
From: Asha Patel <asha@teamnimbus.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Commerce Procurement <procurement@teamnimbus.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity bump & tier remap — Nimbus Commerce

Thanks Marcus — this looks promising. Two quick clarifying questions from procurement:

1) For the soft-burst allowance, will overage billing apply after the buffer or do bursts draw from a separate burst wallet?
2) We need to confirm rate limits (per-second token throttling) for our checkout path — can you guarantee the same latency targets under the new provisioning?

Also please include a line-item for SOC2 evidence and the audit timeline — procurement wants to show that to finance. I'm looping them here.

If possible, can you send a version of the worksheet that includes a blended-cost projection across months and a DocuSign-ready quote?

Best,
Asha Patel
Head of Ops, Nimbus Commerce
asha@teamnimbus.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@teamnimbus.com>
Cc: Nimbus Commerce Procurement <procurement@teamnimbus.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity bump & tier remap — Nimbus Commerce

Hi Asha — appreciate the questions. Quick answers inline and a new attachment with a blended-cost tab and SOC2/evidence line added.

- Soft-burst mechanics: bursts will draw from a separate burst wallet for the first 20% each month; after that standard overage rates apply. We'll include a monthly notification when burn hits 80% of the committed + burst budget.
- Rate limits & latency: we can provision your checkout routes onto a dedicated pool with a 99.9th percentile latency SLO of 120ms (per-token) under expected load. That will require enabling a single-route pin (we've added it to the ops checklist).

I've attached redwood_capacity_plan_v3.xlsx (new blended cost tab) and included a short PDF with SOC2 evidence summary. Proposed next steps:

1) Procurement confirms PO pathway and billing contact.
2) Redwood issues DocuSign quote (30-day net terms indicated; we can change if finance requests).
3) On verbal OK, we pre-allocate capacity and run a smoke test for checkout traffic during your low-traffic window.

If procurement is aligned, I can mark this as a committed deal in the CRM (Deal NBX-4782) and loop Karithik to approve the rateband change.

Thanks — attaching files now.

—Marcus
Attachment: redwood_capacity_plan_v3.xlsx (updated), security-summary-snapshot.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API capacity bump & tier remap — Nimbus Commerce

Marcus / Karthik — quick internal note after reviewing the blended-cost sheet:

- Suggested commercial: 30M monthly commit at list less 18% for first year, with a 3-month trial burst waiver (we absorb first 3 months of burst charges up to the 20% buffer). After month 4 bursts bill to Nimbus.
- Rateband: create Tier-B with 12% discount above 30M, as Marcus suggested. Approve the single-route pin for checkout to meet latency SLOs.
- Accounting ask: if procurement insists on 60-day terms, reduce the discount to 14% — otherwise stick to 18% and keep 30-day net.

Karthik, please confirm capacity provisioning lead time (I think 5 business days once signed). Marissa, can you prep the DocuSign quote with the two term options (30-day / 60-day) and include the SOC2 evidence link in the quote body?

Thanks — will keep this light; expect an answer from Nimbus procurement by early next week.

—Ben
